answers.explanation: Each level refers the resolver one step down the hierarchy until an authoritative server answers.
A is IPv4, AAAA is IPv6.
A resolver that gets a CNAME resolves its target the same way.
NS records are the referrals that walk a resolver down from the root.
Both are cached until their TTL runs out, which keeps the roots from being buried in traffic.
With a long TTL, clients keep using the old address for hours. Short TTLs cost more lookups but let changes spread fast.
Every DNS record carries a TTL in seconds.
It only works well with short TTLs, so clients come back often enough to be spread around.
